preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Deliver one contract-first increment that makes native dense-profile recapture possible while guaranteeing truthful upgrade-choice hierarchy and spatially coherent authored-arena traversal in ordinary release play.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate already contains partial dense-profile plumbing, but the frozen contract remains unqualified because host evidence lacks native 1920x1080 three-cycle receipts. The same loop must also preserve the hard player-facing upgrade-choice and arena-spatial capabilities, so the repair should harmonize their authoritative bindings and provide a deterministic, release-guarded qualification handoff without replacing preserved assets.

stop_conditions: Do not replace or surgically modify the preserved authored cemetery package or retained weapon resources.
Do not add proxy floors, duplicate map geometry, decorative landmark packs, or unrelated wave/audio/HUD systems.
Do not expose tester or validation actions in release exports, and do not treat software-renderer samples as a qualification verdict.
Stop after the candidate-side repair and bounded code checks; GameLoop Runtime and Tester own native recapture, screenshots, and formal closure.

strategy.rationale: Use an explicit isolation strategy rather than repeated transform tuning: make the dense profile a deterministic tester-only contract with complete receipts, then audit the real upgrade-draft presenter and authored spatial contract so visual decisions, collision, visibility, and traversal all bind to authoritative state without changing ordinary run behavior.

code: Run bounded GDScript parse/static checks for every touched script and verify all dense receipt phases, cycle identities, coverage fields, and reset predicates are schema-complete.
Verify release-export guards erase or reject tester_dense/validation actions and no debug overlay, control, or receipt mutates ordinary gameplay.
Verify upgrade projections and rendered rows are capped at three truthful deltas and spatial bindings use the intact authored package with no duplicated or proxy visual geometry.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime and Tester should recapture native 1920x1080 using tester_dense_prepare -> tester_dense_advance -> tester_dense_reset for three serial cycles, collecting renderer/preflight, timing distributions, high-water marks, lifecycle deltas, runtime-error, and next-frame reset-isolation receipts.

During the same host pass, replay ordinary movement around the perimeter and past the central landmark, open an upgrade draft with keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, and verify the selected upgrade state matches the rendered before-to-after values.
Recheck host_godot_boot and native_godot_project preservation while retaining software-renderer evidence as rejected rather than qualified.
visual: Capture shipped gameplay at spawn, a critical route, the central landmark, and a perimeter traversal during dense play; confirm moonlit authored cemetery composition, external depth, readable silhouettes, stable collision, and no pass-through, disappearance, or camera-occlusion drift.

Capture the upgrade page at the configured native/reference viewport and a supported windowed/UI-scale state; confirm icon-led hierarchy, restrained copy, aligned current-to-new values, and complete focus/hover/pressed/disabled/selected states without clipping or opaque debug-style panels.
Confirm dense teardown returns to the ordinary HUD/run state with no visible tester controls, leaked actors, stale effects, or altered progression.

done_when: A deterministic tester-only dense profile supports serial prepare, advance/sample, and reset for 25-40 enemies (target 32), records frame/physics/render timing, active high-churn counts, runtime errors, lifecycle deltas, renderer/preflight status, setup and advance generations, and reset-isolation/next-frame receipts, and remains unavailable in release exports.

The dense profile includes all contract surfaces in its coverage receipt: all three weapon families, pickups, UI, animation, VFX, lights, audio, vitality indicators, and boss presence; three complete retry cycles can be replayed without leaked nodes, timers, signals, pooled actors, audio voices, or progression state.

Upgrade choices are visibly icon/silhouette-led with compact stat icons and truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas; CURRENT never shows NEW or LOCKED placeholders, unchanged/exhaustive rows are omitted, and keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus/hover/pressed/disabled/selected states remain distinct without card reflow or clipping.

The authored arena uses an expand or larger traversable scale contract with an external world or external depth band, keeps the central building or landmark visible and authoritative, and proves movement collision plus visibility stability: no pass-through, disappearance or occlusion drift, and a bounded boundary or perimeter under ordinary movement or movement replay.

Spatial receipts bind spawn, objective, camera coverage, landmark collision, and perimeter bodies to the intact authored package in one transform space; ordinary gameplay remains on native streets/terrain and teardown/reset returns to the same run baseline.

Run snapshot/state exposes the dense handoff and the upgrade/spatial predicates without making UI/effects authoritative; modified scripts/scenes pass bounded parse/static checks and preserve host_godot_boot and native_godot_project structure.
tasks.instructions: Inspect and repair the existing RunController/DenseWaveProfile, UpgradeDraftView, and CemeterySpatialContract bindings as one contract-first pass. Keep ordinary wave progression, automatic combat, authored cemetery composition, and retained weapons unchanged. Add or tighten deterministic tester-only dense setup/sample/reset receipts so host tooling can run native 1920x1080 three-cycle qualification, with renderer gating deferred until samples exist and software sessions retained only as rejected evidence. In the same pass, ensure the real upgrade-draft page and spatial owners satisfy the required player-facing hierarchy and arena integrity directly against runtime state, including the explicit scale, external depth, central landmark collision/occlusion, perimeter, and ordinary movement terms in the acceptance predicates. Prefer wrapper/binding repair and explicit isolation over per-mesh transform edits or asset replacement.
